[I am broadly interested in ensuring a future in which AI reliably advances human well-being. My research develops the science of valid measurement, prediction, and intervention for AI capabilities and risks, combining theory and algorithms to anticipate failures before they occur and improve reliability under real-world conditions and distribution shift. One application area of particular interest is in health and medicine.]{.hero-research}

[I am recruiting PhD students and postdocs for this coming cycle in [ECE](https://ece.illinois.edu/) or [CS](https://siebelschool.illinois.edu/)! More details to come.]{.hero-recruit}

<script>
(function () {
  function drawTimelineRails() {
    var track = document.querySelector('.timeline-track');
    var svg = track && track.querySelector('.timeline-rails');
    if (!track || !svg) return;
    var logos = Array.prototype.slice.call(track.querySelectorAll('.timeline-logo'));
    if (!logos.length) return;

    var tRect = track.getBoundingClientRect();
    var W = track.clientWidth;
    var H = track.clientHeight;

    // Center of each logo, relative to the track.
    var pts = logos.map(function (el) {
      var r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      return { x: r.left - tRect.left + r.width / 2, y: r.top - tRect.top + r.height / 2 };
    });

    // Group into rows by similar vertical center.
    var rows = [];
    pts.forEach(function (p) {
      var row = rows.find(function (g) { return Math.abs(g.y - p.y) < 12; });
      if (!row) { row = { y: p.y, items: [] }; rows.push(row); }
      row.items.push(p);
      row.y = (row.y * (row.items.length - 1) + p.y) / row.items.length;
    });
    rows.sort(function (a, b) { return a.y - b.y; });

    var ns = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';
    svg.setAttribute('viewBox', '0 0 ' + W + ' ' + H);
    svg.setAttribute('width', W);
    svg.setAttribute('height', H);
    while (svg.firstChild) svg.removeChild(svg.firstChild);

    // Shared left→right gradient so colors stay consistent across rows.
    var defs = document.createElementNS(ns, 'defs');
    var grad = document.createElementNS(ns, 'linearGradient');
    grad.setAttribute('id', 'tl-grad');
    grad.setAttribute('gradientUnits', 'userSpaceOnUse');
    grad.setAttribute('x1', 0); grad.setAttribute('y1', 0);
    grad.setAttribute('x2', W); grad.setAttribute('y2', 0);
    [['0', 'rgba(255,95,5,0.55)'], ['1', 'rgba(19,41,75,0.55)']].forEach(function (s) {
      var stop = document.createElementNS(ns, 'stop');
      stop.setAttribute('offset', s[0]); stop.setAttribute('stop-color', s[1]);
      grad.appendChild(stop);
    });
    defs.appendChild(grad);
    svg.appendChild(defs);

    rows.forEach(function (row, r) {
      var xStart = (r === 0) ? row.items[0].x : 0;
      var xEnd = (r === rows.length - 1) ? row.items[row.items.length - 1].x : W;
      var line = document.createElementNS(ns, 'line');
      line.setAttribute('x1', xStart); line.setAttribute('y1', row.y);
      line.setAttribute('x2', xEnd); line.setAttribute('y2', row.y);
      line.setAttribute('stroke', 'url(#tl-grad)');
      line.setAttribute('stroke-width', '2');
      line.setAttribute('stroke-linecap', 'round');
      svg.appendChild(line);
    });
  }

  var scheduled = false;
  function schedule() {
    if (scheduled) return;
    scheduled = true;
    requestAnimationFrame(function () { scheduled = false; drawTimelineRails(); });
  }

  if (document.readyState !== 'loading') schedule();
  else document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', schedule);
  window.addEventListener('load', schedule);
  window.addEventListener('resize', schedule);
  if (window.ResizeObserver) {
    var t = document.querySelector('.timeline-track');
    if (t) new ResizeObserver(schedule).observe(t);
  }
})();
</script>

::: {.bio-tabs-panel .bio-tabs-panel-1}

Olawale (Wale) Salaudeen is an incoming Assistant Professor at the [University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign](https://illinois.edu/) and a Postdoctoral Researcher at [Microsoft Research](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/lab/microsoft-research-new-york/) on the [FATE](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/group/fate/) team. He was previously an AI Center Fellow in Residence at [Schmidt Sciences](https://www.schmidtsciences.org/), a Postdoctoral Researcher at [MIT](https://www.mit.edu/) in the [Healthy ML Lab](https://healthyml.org/), and a Postdoctoral Scholar at the [Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center](https://www.ericandwendyschmidtcenter.org/) at the [Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard](https://www.broadinstitute.org/). Before his postdoctoral positions, he earned a Ph.D. in Computer Science from the [University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign](https://cs.illinois.edu/) and the [Stanford Trustworthy AI Research (STAIR) Lab](https://stair.cs.stanford.edu/) at [Stanford University](https://www.stanford.edu/).

His research develops the science of valid measurement, prediction, and intervention for AI capabilities and risks, combining theory and algorithms to anticipate failures before they occur and improve reliability under real-world conditions and distribution shift. His work has been published in leading AI and ML venues and recognized with paper awards, including a Best Paper Award at the NeurIPS 2025 Workshop on Evaluating the Evolving LLM Lifecycle, as well as media coverage.

He has received a Sloan Scholarship, a Beckman Graduate Research Fellowship, a GEM Associate Fellowship, and an NSF Miniature Brain Machinery Traineeship. He has interned at Sandia National Laboratories, Google Brain, Cruise LLC, and the [Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems](https://is.mpg.de/). He received a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering with minors in Computer Science and Mathematics from [Texas A&M University](https://www.tamu.edu/).

:::

## Selected Research Directions

::: {.direction-grid}

::: {.direction-box}
### Valid Measurement and Prediction of AI Capabilities and Risks

AI systems exhibit jagged intelligence---they excel at some tasks but fail at others that share a common human capability, exhibiting seemingly incongruous behaviors. I develop the science of identifying and measuring AI-specific latent traits, capabilities, and risks to enable less jagged, more predictable behaviors across real-world settings.

::: {.direction-papers}
- [AI Construct Lexis.](https://aiconstructlexis.github.io/) *In Review*
- [Measurement to Meaning: A Validity-Centered Framework for AI Evaluation.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10573) *In Review* [(preliminary in NeurIPS 2025 Workshop on Evaluating the Evolving LLM Lifecycle)]{.pub-note-info}
- [Stop Evaluating AI with Human Tests, Develop Principled, AI-specific Tests instead.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.23009) *ICML 2026 (Position Paper Track)*
- [Toward an Evaluation Science for Generative AI Systems.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05336) *The Bridge, NAE 2025*
- [On Evaluating Methods vs. Evaluating Models.](https://openreview.net/forum?id=8yg3XadfIZ) *NeurIPS 2025 Workshop on Evaluating the Evolving LLM Lifecycle* [(Best Paper)]{.pub-note}
:::
:::

::: {.direction-box}
### Characterizing and Intervening on Causal and Spurious Mechanisms of AI Behavior

AI systems often rely on spurious, unexpected mechanisms of behavior, performing well in training environments but failing when conditions shift. I develop algorithms to identify and disentangle causal from spurious mechanisms so models rely on stable, causal patterns instead.

::: {.direction-papers}
- [Are Domain Generalization Benchmarks with Accuracy on the Line Misspecified?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00186) *TMLR 2025* [(J2C)]{.pub-note} *+ ICLR 2026 Journal Track*
- [ImageNot: A Contrast with ImageNet Preserves Model Rankings.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02112) *TMLR 2026*
- [Aggregation Hides OOD Generalization Failures from Spurious Correlations.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.24884) *NeurIPS 2025* [(Spotlight)]{.pub-note}
- [Causally Inspired Regularization Enables Domain General Representations.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16277) *AISTATS 2024*
- [On Domain Generalization Datasets as Proxy Benchmarks for Causal Representation Learning.](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=LbFK9pUlA5) *NeurIPS 2024 CRL Workshop* [(Oral)]{.pub-note}
:::
:::

::: {.direction-box}
### Statistical Foundations of Inference-Time Adaptation of AI Systems

AI behaviors often become unreliable when deployment conditions change. I develop methods that use proxy variables and concept-based representations to adapt model behavior at inference time, without retraining.

::: {.direction-papers}
- [Adapting to Latent Subgroup Shifts via Concepts and Proxies.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v206/alabdulmohsin23a.html) *AISTATS 2023*
- [Proxy Methods for Domain Adaptation.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.07442) *AISTATS 2024*
- [Improving Single-round Active Adaptation: A Prediction Variability Perspective.](https://openreview.net/forum?id=Vthqn5VE7L) *TMLR 2025*
:::
:::

::: {.direction-box}
### Measuring and Steering Societal Impacts

AI systems can behave inequitably across the populations they serve, through biased data or learning objectives misaligned with user welfare. I develop tools to measure these disparities and methods to mitigate them in deployed systems.

::: {.direction-papers}
- Avoiding Common Failures in AI for Health and Medicine. *Cell 2026* [(Review Article, To appear)]{.pub-note-info}
- [Understanding Challenges to the Interpretation of Disaggregated Evaluations of Algorithmic Fairness.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.04193) *NeurIPS 2025*
- [On Group Sufficiency Under Label Bias.](https://openreview.net/forum?id=xRb0taq0pD) *NeurIPS 2025*
- [What's in a Query: Polarity-Aware Distribution-Based Fair Ranking.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11429) *WWW 2025*
:::
:::

## Mentoring

I am happy to mentor students with overlapping research interests. Particularly for undergrads at MIT, programs like [UROP](https://urop.mit.edu/) are a great mechanism for mentorship. I am also very happy to give advice on applying to and navigating graduate programs in computer science, especially for those to whom this type of guidance would be otherwise unavailable.

:::
